pairs.evidence: scripts/dev-guard.mjs:121 The dev-guard worker-storm breaker is the only process sampler running alongside the dev build. When the PowerShell or pgrep probe fails or times out, it reports 0 node processes instead of reporting the failure, so a broken sampler looks exactly like 'no storm' and the breaker silently never trips.

techniques.evidence: scripts/dev-guard.mjs:121 Breaks 'instrument failure is loud': a probe failure collapses to 0, which reads as good news. The sampler also counts every node process on the machine against a launch baseline, not the guard's own process tree.

scripts/dev-empty.mjs:12 dev-empty names a reaper for its throwaway DB on every launch, but no tracked script prunes or byte-budgets the .next-empty dist/turbopack cache that the same run creates. A grep for prune/.next-empty under scripts found only lock checks and a perf skip-list.

scripts/dev-inspector/source-loc-loader.cjs:29 The heavy Babel stamping pass is opt-in and additive. @babel/core is required lazily, so it stays absent from the default dev and production builds. The gated side is kept alive by the source-loc-loader fixtures that test:docs runs.

scripts/dev-empty.mjs:21 Plain `npm run dev` is the lite default. dev:empty deliberately defaults to the expensive inspector variant and states why (who uses it) and what it costs, with an explicit --no-inspect opt-out that overrides an inherited DEV_INSPECT.

scripts/dev-empty.mjs:16 Who shares a build directory under concurrency is decided explicitly: a second dev server always gets its own distDir instead of racing the seeded server's .next lock. Stale lock holders are reaped by signature, not by process name.
